rationale: The golden submission (trojan_present=true, suspect_flops={u_priv_ff1,u_priv_ff2}, correct reset_net_summary and description) is rejected by evaluate.py solely on SR5: golden_run.ok=false with exit non-zero because the SR5 simulation-derived persistent flop set is computed as {u_ctrl_ff2, u_dp_ff5} instead of {u_priv_ff1, u_priv_ff2}. All FR1-4 and SR1-4 pass for the golden, confirming the netlist and golden answer are structurally and semantically correct; the defect is isolated to the SR5 cross-check stimulus/classification logic in tb_cross_check.v and/or evaluate.py's check_sr5, which does not reproduce the documented ground-truth reset-polarity anomaly in simulation. Because SR5 is currently a hard gate on overall pass/fail, no correct submission can pass, which blocks the differential harness and forces mutation_score=0.0 with mutation_status=blocked_by_differential (not a meaningful signal). This is a textbook golden_rejected evaluator bug, not a case_artifacts defect: the netlist wiring, testbench structure, and golden report all correctly reflect the hidden ground truth per acceptance_criteria.
revision_instructions: Fix the SR5 cross-check so it corroborates the correct suspect set on the real netlist, and stop it from hard-gating overall PASS/FAIL. Concretely: (1) In tb_cross_check.v and/or evaluate.py's check_sr5, verify that the reset-pulse stimulus actually drives the control and datapath registers to non-zero values before the reset pulse so their post-reset clearing is observable, and that the persistence classification logic (comparing pre-reset and post-reset flop values through the pinned CLK/RSTN/DIN/CTRL/DOUT interface) correctly identifies which flops fail to clear when reset is asserted. Debug why the current stimulus/classification reports u_ctrl_ff2 and u_dp_ff5 as persistent instead of u_priv_ff1 and u_priv_ff2 — likely the stimulus drives those particular control/datapath registers to values that coincidentally hold post-reset (e.g. their next-state function evaluates to the same value under reset-cleared upstream state), or the classification incorrectly flags any flop whose post-reset value equals its pre-reset value (which can spuriously include flops that legitimately reset to a value equal to their prior state) rather than checking against the documented all-zero reset value for every flop. The check should assert that every correctly-reset flop reaches its defined all-zero reset value after the pulse, and separately flag any flop that fails to reach zero despite reset being asserted; that failure set is what must match the structurally-derived suspect set. (2) Per the hidden spec's own description of SR5 as 'a bonus/consistency signal, not solely for PASS/FAIL', change evaluate.py so SR5 failure alone does not fail the overall submission when SR1-SR4 and FR1-FR4 already pass; keep it as an informational/corroboration check that does not gate exit code. (3) After the fix, re-run the golden submission end-to-end and confirm all [TEST] PASS lines and exit code 0, and confirm the naive/empty baseline still fails at least SR1/SR2/SR3/SR4 as before.
